witness.description: Explicit arithmetic progression of primes inside {1,...,N}, certifying the finite-instance content of the Maynard-type prime-AP lower bound on a bounded range. Progression: 5, 11, 17, 23, 29 (first term 5, common difference 6), length k=5, all primes, all within N=30.

claim: Successful return (no exception) establishes the finite-instance content of lemma L1's lower-bound mathematics: an explicit arithmetic progression of 5 primes inside {1,...,30}, verified by exact integer arithmetic. The verifier has the required def verify(witness) entrypoint, raises on every failed check, uses no imports and no I/O, is deterministic and fail-closed. This is a FRAGMENT: it certifies concrete instantiation of the Maynard-type lower-bound phenomenon and is consistent with both the affirmative o(log N) close and its negation — exactly L1's stated non_result character. The infinite-quantifier asymptotic statement itself is NOT covered.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
